identity_provider.name: Identity Provider (Okta / Azure AD / Google Workspace)
identity_provider.what_to_provide: Admin console: configured apps with SSO, MFA enforcement policy, user/group config, role assignments, recently deactivated users, service account list
identity_provider.notes: Highest-value evidence source. One well-configured IdP covers 7 controls and 8 objectives.

hr_system_records.name: HR System / Records
hr_system_records.what_to_provide: Background check policy + completion records; offboarding checklist with access revocation timestamps; training completion records; performance review template; job descriptions; Code of Conduct acknowledgments; key person analysis; cross-training records
hr_system_records.notes: Covers all of People controls. Offboarding records overlap with IAM-04 (deprovisioning).

security_policy_library.name: Security Policy Library
security_policy_library.what_to_provide: Complete policy library: Access Control, Change Management, Incident Response, Data Protection, Acceptable Use, Vendor Management, Risk Management, Business Continuity. Plus procedures/runbooks. Version history, approval records, ownership matrix.
security_policy_library.notes: Foundational evidence. CC5.3 is implicitly tested for every other control — if a process lacks a backing policy, that's a gap here.

risk_assessment_document.name: Risk Assessment Document
risk_assessment_document.what_to_provide: Annual risk assessment: threats, vulnerabilities, likelihood/impact, risk responses, vendor risk section, fraud risk section, change impact assessment, risk-to-control mapping
risk_assessment_document.notes: One document covers 7 objectives across CC3 and CC5. Most impactful single document after policies.

version_control_git.name: Version Control (Git) + CI/CD Pipeline
version_control_git.what_to_provide: Merged PRs: description, code review, CI test results, approval, merge. Pipeline config: automated tests, deployment stages, branch protection rules.
version_control_git.notes: Git + CI/CD covers all of Change Management. A well-configured pipeline with branch protection is complete evidence for OBJ-8.1.1.

cloud_provider_console.name: Cloud Provider Console (AWS / GCP / Azure)
cloud_provider_console.what_to_provide: VPC/network config; security group rules; encryption settings (RDS, S3, etc.); KMS keys; backup config; auto-scaling; multi-AZ/region setup; IAM policies; CloudTrail/audit log config
cloud_provider_console.notes: Richest infrastructure evidence source. Covers network, encryption, backups, capacity, hardening, and logging.

vulnerability_scanner.name: Vulnerability Scanner (Qualys / Nessus / etc.)
vulnerability_scanner.what_to_provide: Recent scan reports; scan schedule; remediation tracking with SLA compliance; scanner coverage
vulnerability_scanner.notes: Scan reports serve dual purpose: vulnerability management and ongoing monitoring evidence.

penetration_test_report.name: Penetration Test Report
penetration_test_report.what_to_provide: Annual pen test report; remediation status for findings; re-test confirmation for critical/high findings
penetration_test_report.notes: Annual pen test: standalone evidence but heavily weighted by buyers. Also serves as 'separate evaluation' for CC4.1.

siem_log_management.name: SIEM / Log Management (Datadog / Splunk / CloudTrail)
siem_log_management.what_to_provide: Dashboard showing log sources; alert rule definitions; retention config; event triage process; on-call rotation; escalation records
siem_log_management.notes: Covers all of CC7.2-7.3 (monitoring and event evaluation).

endpoint_management.name: Endpoint Management (MDM / EDR)
endpoint_management.what_to_provide: MDM dashboard: enrolled devices, compliance status, enforced policies (encryption, screen lock, updates). EDR: deployment coverage, threat detection records.
endpoint_management.notes: MDM/EDR dashboard is definitive evidence for endpoint security (CC6.1 partial, CC6.8).

incident_records.name: Incident Records
incident_records.what_to_provide: IR Plan document; IR team roster; tabletop exercise notes; incident tickets/reports (if any); post-mortems; control improvements post-incident
incident_records.notes: If no incidents during period: IR plan + tabletop + roster are the evidence. If incidents occurred: include full documentation.

vendor_documentation.name: Vendor Documentation
vendor_documentation.what_to_provide: Vendor inventory with risk tiers; assessment questionnaires; contracts with security clauses; subservice org SOC 2 reports; CSOC documentation
vendor_documentation.notes: Subservice org SOC 2 reports (AWS, cloud providers) are the most critical items. Don't forget CSOC documentation.

bcp_drp_backup_tests.name: BCP/DRP + Backup Tests
bcp_drp_backup_tests.what_to_provide: BCP/DRP document; RTO/RPO definitions; DR test results; backup restoration test results; backup monitoring dashboard; multi-region architecture evidence
bcp_drp_backup_tests.notes: Covers CC9.1 and A1.2-A1.3 simultaneously. Key: TESTING evidence, not just the plan document.

governance_org_documentation.name: Governance & Org Documentation
governance_org_documentation.what_to_provide: Org chart; leadership/board meeting minutes; security program review notes; governance charter; SoD analysis; RACI matrix
governance_org_documentation.notes: Often simple to produce but frequently missing for startups. Meeting minutes are critical for CC1.2.

customer_facing_documentation.name: Customer-Facing Documentation
customer_facing_documentation.what_to_provide: Terms of service; SLAs; privacy policy; trust/security page; CUEC documentation; security@ contact; responsible disclosure policy; status page
customer_facing_documentation.notes: Usually already published online. Quick to collect and verify.

deficiency_issue_tracking.name: Deficiency & Issue Tracking
deficiency_issue_tracking.what_to_provide: Issue tracker: identified deficiencies, severity classification, assignments, remediation status, resolution dates, SLA compliance; management/board reporting on significant deficiencies
deficiency_issue_tracking.notes: Can be a spreadsheet or Jira/Linear. Key: showing the identify-assign-track-resolve-report cycle.

asset_data_management.name: Asset Inventory & Data Classification
asset_data_management.what_to_provide: Asset inventory: hardware, software, cloud services, data assets with owners. Data classification scheme with handling requirements. Data flow diagrams.
asset_data_management.notes: Asset inventory + data classification are foundational for CC2.1. Data disposal and retention are often documented in the data retention policy.

secure_development_lifecycle.name: Secure Development Lifecycle (SDLC)
secure_development_lifecycle.what_to_provide: SDLC policy or documented process; code scanning (SAST/DAST) configs and results; dependency scanning (Dependabot, Snyk); security architecture reviews for significant changes.
secure_development_lifecycle.notes: CHG-04 (secure development) and CHG-05 (security architecture review) cover the security-specific aspects of change management.

service_account_management.name: Service Account & API Key Inventory
service_account_management.what_to_provide: Service account inventory: name, purpose, owner, permissions, creation date, last rotation date. API key inventory. Rotation compliance status.
service_account_management.notes: Often discovered during access reviews. Key finding: unrotated keys, overprivileged service accounts.

privacy_documentation.name: Privacy Documentation (ROPA, DPAs, Consent)
privacy_documentation.what_to_provide: Privacy policy, ROPA (record of processing activities), DPAs with processors, consent mechanisms, DSAR process, breach notification procedures, data subject rights implementation.
privacy_documentation.notes: Only applicable when Privacy TSC is in scope. All 10 privacy controls are covered by the combined privacy documentation package.

physical_security.name: Physical Security (Offices / Data Centers)
physical_security.what_to_provide: Physical access controls: badge system logs, visitor logs, restricted area identification, termination physical access removal evidence.
physical_security.notes: Usually N/A for cloud-only remote companies. For WeWork/shared offices, document the CSOC relationship.

llm_provider_console.name: AI Model Provider Console (OpenAI / Anthropic / etc.)
llm_provider_console.what_to_provide: Org-level data-controls settings showing training and retention posture, executed agreements or DPAs per provider, the provider inventory, and where prompts/outputs are logged.
